outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Foundations of Efficient Model Adaptation
outline.description: The landscape of artificial intelligence has undergone a seismic shift with the advent of large foundation models, such as ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion. These systems exhibit remarkable generalization capabilities across a vast array of tasks, driven by architectures containing hundreds of billions of parameters. For instance, models like GPT-3 possess approximately 175 billion parameters, a scale that renders the traditional practice of training a model from scratch prohibitively expensive for most researchers and organizations. outline.description: The pursuit of parameter efficiency in fine-tuning large foundation models often forces a trade-off between the expressivity of the learned transformations and the computational resources required to store them. In the context of Orthogonal Fine-tuning (OFT), the challenge lies in constructing a dense orthogonal matrix that can effectively rotate the feature space of a pretrained model without exploding the number of trainable parameters. Traditional approaches, such as using a full dense orthogonal matrix, require $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ parameters for a dimension $d$, which is prohibitive for modern architectures. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Butterfly Structures and Fast Linear Transforms
outline.description: The quest for computational efficiency in handling large-scale data transformations dates back decades, culminating in one of the most influential algorithms in modern science: the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Before this breakthrough, computing the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) required a direct matrix-vector multiplication involving a dense matrix of size $N \times N$, resulting in a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$. For large datasets, this quadratic growth rendered real-time signal processing and spectral analysis practically impossible.
